messages.content: Honestly break down, in detail, how someone can actually tell if they're in a healthy relationship versus one that just looks good from outside.

Honestly, the outside view is genuinely unreliable for this because relationships are performed differently in public than they're lived in private - so the real signals are internal ones. First, actually notice how you feel after spending time with your partner: energized and like yourself, or drained and like you're managing them. Second, honestly examine conflict - not whether it happens, since all real relationships have it, but whether it resolves toward understanding or just repeats the same fight with new words. Third, actually check whether you can be fully yourself, including the less impressive parts, without fear of punishment or withdrawal of affection - relationships that only work when you're performing a good version of yourself aren't actually safe. Finally, honestly ask whether your individual life outside the relationship (friends, goals, interests) has grown or shrunk since being together - a healthy relationship generally expands your life, an unhealthy one slowly narrows it, even when it looks fine to everyone watching from outside.
